## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Niyāmokkantikathā* (Kv 4.8) is a controversy located in the fourth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Dube 1980]. The title designates the debate concerning "stepping into the path destined to reach Nibbana or Assurance" (*niyāmokkanti*) [Dube 1980]. The doctrinal contention centres upon whether a Bodhisatta is assured of reaching Nibbāna prior to their final birth, a subject disputed by a certain section of early Buddhists [Dube 1980]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language for this text [SuttaCentral].
Both curated parallels and text-reuse analyses connect Kv 4.8 closely with accounts of the Buddha's quest for awakening. SuttaCentral notes references and parallels in the *Pāsarāsi Sutta* (MN 26), the *Bodhirājakumāra Sutta* (MN 85), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and Dhammapada verse 353, alongside cross-tradition parallels such as the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu*, the *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, the *Lalitavistara*, the *Udānavarga*, and Chinese versions in the Taishō canon (T 210, T 212, T 213) [SuttaCentral].
According to DharmaNexus, the text shares 556 matching passages with 40 other Pali texts, exhibiting substantial internal text reuse with the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), the *Paṭisambhidākathā* (Ps 2.6), other Kathāvatthu debates (such as Kv 23.3 and Kv 20.6), the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and particularly with MN 26 and MN 85 (sharing §15.3–21.4 with 0.98 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns sections of Kv 4.8 with Sanskrit sources (including the *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, the Subaši *Udānavarga*, the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and the *Mahāvastu*), Tibetan texts (the *Udānavarga*, *Abhiniṣkramaṇasūtra*, and *Lalitavistara*), and Chinese Āgamas (the *Madhyama-āgama* T 26 and *Ekottarika-āgama* T 125) [DharmaNexus]. Where DharmaNexus and SuttaCentral identify corresponding Sanskrit, Tibetan, Chinese, and Vinaya/Sutta materials, their findings corroborate one another [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
